text: Last lesson showed you the SHAPE of a plan — seek versus scan. But a shape isn't a number. To prove a tuning change actually helped, you need real measurements. That's what these two SET options give you.

SET STATISTICS TIME ON prints two numbers into the Messages tab every time you run a query: CPU time, how much processor work it actually consumed, and elapsed time, the total wall-clock time including any waiting. If those two numbers are close, the query was CPU-bound. If elapsed time is much higher, something else — disk, locks, other queries — is the real bottleneck, not the query's logic.

SET STATISTICS IO ON prints, per table touched, logical reads — pages read from the buffer cache — and physical reads, pages that had to come from disk because they weren't cached. Logical reads is the number to watch. Unlike timing, it doesn't jitter with how busy the server happens to be — it's a direct, stable measure of how much work the storage engine did.

Here's why that matters. Run a query, note the logical reads — say, fifteen, because it's scanning. Add a covering index. Run the exact same query again. The logical reads drops sharply. That drop is the proof the index change genuinely reduced the work — not a guess, not a feeling, a number you can put in a ticket.

Time can lie to you depending on server load. Logical reads almost never does. Next lesson: SET STATISTICS PROFILE and the execution plan as XML — getting the plan itself back as data you can query and save. See you there.
